key_insight: In a retrospective evaluation, LabARIA’s multi-agent AI flagged laboratory quality issues before 96.4% of recorded QC actions, with a median lead time of 5.40 days.
clinical_relevance: Integrated monitoring could help laboratory teams identify specimen, analytical quality, and workflow problems earlier, although patient-care benefits remain unproven.
method: Coordinated AI agents analyzed specimen workflows, internal quality control, and laboratory operations.
Patient-based real-time quality control selected monitoring strategies across 35 analytes.
A dashboard and chatbot presented alerts and summaries for human review.
evidence_signal: Single-center retrospective evaluation included 177,480 specimen-panel records, 75,103 IQC measurements, and 422 QC actions; adding patient-based monitoring increased action recall from 0.964 to 0.993.
watch_item: Prospective validation is needed: retrospective action recall does not establish clinical benefit or false-alert burden, and forecasting used controlled perturbations and synthetic operational data.
paper_title: LabARIA: A Multi-Agent System for Integrative Analytics in Clinical Laboratories
